ai.text:
The European Union is proposing a new funding programme, the Single Market and Customs Programme, to run from 2028 to 2034. It would combine four older programmes covering the Single Market, the Customs Union, taxation and anti-fraud work, and it would also support the development and sharing of European statistics. The aim is to make these policy areas work together more consistently, reduce fragmented funding rules, and simplify how the programme is carried out. The European Parliament would decide on the proposal under the ordinary legislative procedure, on an equal footing with the Council.

The overall goal is to strengthen a competitive Single Market and a strong Customs Union while protecting the financial and economic interests and security of the Union and its Member States. The programme is meant to be flexible and simple to run, and to support the Union's wider policy priorities.

It has several specific aims. One is to help citizens, consumers, investors and businesses make informed decisions and use the opportunities of the Single Market for goods, people, services and capital, including by improving digital and financial literacy and supporting access to redress. Another is to strengthen cooperation between national authorities, the Commission and other EU bodies, including on crisis response, and to build up the capacity of national authorities, including customs and tax authorities, and the shared digital solutions they use.

The programme would also support harmonised standards and the uniform application and enforcement of EU law, and help customs authorities work together as one. It aims to ensure effective market surveillance, consumer protection, product conformity and safety. In addition, it would protect the Union's financial and other interests from fraud, corruption and other illegal activity, support tax policy and tax collection, and encourage evidence-based, digitally ready policymaking. Finally, it would provide relevant and comparable official European statistics.

The proposal sets a budget of EUR 6.238 million, in current prices, for the 2028 to 2034 period.
